drivingQuestion: What does the word ויחל teach about Moses' prayer for Israel after the Golden Calf?
outcomeNote: Five readings of ויחל are set side by side and none is refuted or preferred; only the terminological questions on אחילו are settled.

segments.he: ״וַיְחַל מֹשֶׁה אֶת פְּנֵי ה׳״, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָמַד מֹשֶׁה בִּתְפִלָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, עַד שֶׁהֶחֱלָהוּ. וְרָבָא אָמַר: עַד שֶׁהֵפֵר לוֹ נִדְרוֹ. כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וַיְחַל״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״לֹא יַחֵל דְּבָרוֹ״, וְאָמַר מָר: הוּא אֵינוֹ מֵיחֵל, אֲבָל אֲחֵרִים מְחִלִּין לוֹ.
segments.en: The Torah continues: «“And Moses beseeched [vayḥal] before the Lord”» (Exodus 32:11). Many interpretations were given for this uncommon term, vayḥal: «Rabbi Elazar said:» It «teaches that Moses stood in prayer before the Holy One, Blessed be He, until it made him ill [»heḥelahu«]» from overexertion. «And Rava said:» Moses stood in prayer «until he nullified His vow,» as the term vayḥal alludes to nullification of an oath. «Here it is written vayḥal, and there» referring to vows, «it is written: “He shall not nullify [lo yaḥel] his word”» (Numbers 30:3). «And» with regard to vows, «the Master said: He» who vowed «cannot nullify» his vow, «but others,» the court, «can nullify» his vow «for him.» Here, it is as if Moses nullified the Lord’s vow to destroy Israel.

segments.he: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמָּסַר עַצְמוֹ לְמִיתָה עֲלֵיהֶם. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִם אַיִן מְחֵנִי נָא מִסִּפְרְךָ״.
segments.en: «And Shmuel said:» The term vayḥal «teaches that» Moses «gave his life,» from the term ḥalal, a dead person, «for» Israel, «as it is stated: “And if not, erase me, please, from Your book”» (Exodus 32:32).

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֻחֲלָה עֲלֵיהֶם מִדַּת רַחֲמִים.
segments.en: «Rava,» also interpreting this verse, «said» that «Rav Yitzḥak said:» The term vayḥal «teaches that he caused the Divine Attribute of Mercy to take effect [heḥela] upon them.»

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! חוּלִּין הוּא לְּךָ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis say» that this term constitutes the essence of Moses’ claim: «It teaches that Moses said before the Holy One Blessed be He: Master of the Universe! It is a sacrilege [ḥullin] for You to do something like this.»

segments.he: ״וַיְחַל מֹשֶׁה אֶת פְּנֵי ה׳״, תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָמַד מֹשֶׁה בִּתְפִלָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַד שֶׁאֲחָזַתּוּ אֲחִילוּ. מַאי אֲחִילוּ? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת. מַאי אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִשָּׁתָא דְגַרְמֵי.
segments.en: And another interpretation of the verse, «“And Moses beseeched [vayḥal] before the Lord.” It was taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: This» term «teaches that Moses stood in prayer before the Holy One, Blessed be He, until he was overcome by aḥilu.» Even the Sages were unfamiliar with this term. Therefore, the Gemara asks: «What is» the meaning of «aḥilu? Rabbi Elazar,» an amora of Eretz Yisrael, «said» that aḥilu is «fire in the bones.» However, this expression was familiar in Eretz Yisrael but not in Babylonia. They asked in Babylonia: «What is» the disease that they called «fire of the bones? Abaye said» that is a disease known in Babylonia as «eshta degarmei,» which in Aramaic means «fire of the bones;» in other words, a fever.

segments.he: ״זְכֹר לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לָהֶם בָּךְ״. מַאי ״בָּךְ״? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, אִלְמָלֵא נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לָהֶם בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ, הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁשָּׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ בְּטֵלִים — כָּךְ שְׁבוּעָתְךָ בְּטֵלָה. וְעַכְשָׁו שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּעְתָּ לָהֶם בְּשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל, מָה שִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל חַי וְקַיָּים לְעוֹלָם וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים — כָּךְ שְׁבוּעָתְךָ קַיֶּימֶת לְעוֹלָם וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים.
segments.en: As Moses continues his prayer, he says: «“Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel Your servants, to whom You swore in Your name”» (Exodus 32:13). «What is» the meaning of «in Your name? Rabbi Elazar said: Moses said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, had You sworn to them by the heavens and the earth, I would say: Just as the heavens and the earth will» ultimately «be no more, so too Your oath will be null and void. Now that You swore to them by Your great name, just as Your name lives and stands for all eternity, so too does Your oath live and stand for all eternity.»

moves.summary: the verse ויחל משה is taken up as the lemma for a chain of readings
moves.about: the verse ויחל משה, taken up as the lemma

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: מלמד שעמד משה בתפלה
moves.summary: ויחל means Moses prayed until the effort made him ill
moves.about: ויחל means Moses prayed until he made himself ill

moves.cueHe: ורבא אמר: עד שהפר לו נדרו
moves.summary: Rava reads ויחל as annulment: Moses annulled God's vow to destroy Israel
moves.about: ויחל means Moses annulled God's vow, by a gezera shava with לא יחל דברו

moves.cueHe: כתיב הכא ״ויחל״, וכתיב התם ״לא יחל דברו״
moves.summary: a gezera shava with the law of vows, plus the rule that others may annul a vow for the vower
moves.about: the second limb of the gezera shava, from the law of vows

moves.cueHe: ושמואל אמר: מלמד שמסר עצמו למיתה עליהם
moves.summary: Shmuel reads ויחל from ḥalal: Moses gave his life for Israel
moves.about: ויחל means Moses gave himself over to death for Israel

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא אמר רב יצחק: מלמד שהחלה עליהם מדת רחמים
moves.summary: in Rav Yitzḥak's name: Moses brought the attribute of mercy to rest upon Israel
moves.about: the reading that ויחל means Moses brought the attribute of mercy to rest on Israel

moves.cueHe: ורבנן אמרי: מלמד שאמר משה לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא
moves.summary: the Rabbis read ויחל as ḥullin: Moses said that destroying Israel would profane God's name
moves.about: ויחל carries Moses' claim that destroying Israel would be a profanation for God

moves.summary: a baraita gives a tannaitic form of the first reading: Moses prayed until aḥilu seized him
moves.about: a baraita of R' Eliezer the Great on the word ויחל

moves.summary: the Gemara asks what the baraita's word אחילו means
moves.about: the meaning of the word אחילו in the baraita

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: אש של עצמות
moves.summary: R' Elazar glosses it as fire of the bones
moves.about: glossing the baraita's אחילו as fire of the bones

moves.summary: the Babylonians in turn ask what fire of the bones means
moves.about: the meaning of the Eretz Yisrael idiom אש של עצמות, unfamiliar in Babylonia

moves.summary: Abaye identifies it with the Babylonian אשתא דגרמי, a fever
moves.about: glossing אש של עצמות as the Babylonian אשתא דגרמי, a fever

moves.cueHe: ״זכר לאברהם ליצחק ולישראל עבדיך אשר נשבעת להם בך״
moves.summary: the next verse of Moses' prayer is taken up
moves.about: the next verse of Moses' prayer, taken up as a lemma

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: אמר משה לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא
moves.summary: an oath sworn by God's own eternal name, unlike one sworn by heaven and earth, can never be void
moves.about: בך shows the oath was sworn by God's own eternal name and so cannot lapse

moves.summary: the Gemara asks what בך adds
moves.about: what the word בך in the verse adds
